recent_posts.title: Analyze cloud costs with flexible spreadsheets in Datadog Sheets
recent_posts.summary: Datadog Sheets combined with Cloud Cost Management (CCM) lets FinOps teams analyze live cloud cost data using spreadsheet-style tabs with formulas, pivot tables, and calculated columns. Key use cases include tracking monthly cloud spend by provider with currency conversion, forecasting yearly cloud budgets by team with growth assumptions, and building connected cost analysis workflows without exporting data to external tools. A preview of flexible spreadsheet tabs is available with a templates gallery for common cloud cost scenarios.

recent_posts.title: Connect triage and investigation in a single workflow with Datadog Cloud SIEM
recent_posts.summary: Datadog Cloud SIEM now connects triage and investigation in a single workflow, eliminating the need to switch between multiple tools. Analysts can view case context directly in the Signal Explorer, escalate signals into structured cases with auto-populated metadata, and manage the full investigation lifecycle within Datadog. Bidirectional syncing with Jira and ServiceNow keeps tickets in sync, while Slack thread replies are automatically added to case timelines. Automation rules can trigger case creation for high-severity signals and execute response workflows including remediation runbooks and custom agents.

recent_posts.title: Inside Datadog's AI Research Lab: Two PhD candidates behind Toto
recent_posts.summary: Datadog's AI Research Lab in Paris hosts PhD candidates Viktoriya Zhukova and Salahidine Lemaachi through France's CIFRE program. Viktoriya researches multimodal timeseries forecasting, leveraging Datadog's vast observability datasets to improve prediction accuracy. Salahidine focuses on world models at the intersection of foundation models and AI observability, including using topological data for anomaly detection. Both contributed to Toto, Datadog's open-source timeseries foundation model presented at NeurIPS 2025 with over 9 million downloads, which has been deployed in production for cloud cost forecasting. The post highlights how Paris's strong academic ecosystem and France's R&D incentives make it an ideal environment for applied AI research.

recent_posts.title: This Month in Datadog - April 2026
recent_posts.summary: Datadog's April 2026 monthly roundup covers several new product features: the Datadog MCP Server giving AI agents real-time access to observability data, Datadog Experiments for measuring product change impact on user journeys, Bits AI Security Analyst for autonomous Cloud SIEM investigations, and Bits AI Dev Agent for Code Security that auto-generates vulnerability fixes submittable as GitHub pull requests. Additional updates include Bits Assistant for natural language exploration, Bits AI SRE deeper reasoning, an updated Host Map, AI summaries for session replays, a Governance Console, and natural language metric queries.

recent_posts.title: Add dynamically updating context to logs with Reference Tables and Observability Pipelines
recent_posts.summary: Datadog Observability Pipelines now supports centralized log enrichment using Reference Tables that dynamically sync with external data sources like Snowflake, ServiceNow CMDB, Salesforce, Databricks, and cloud storage (S3, Azure Blob, GCS). The Enrichment Table processor attaches fresh metadata to logs before routing them to SIEMs or data lakes, eliminating duplicate lookups in downstream tools. The workflow supports rehydrating archived logs with current context for threat investigations, and enables smart conditional routing based on enriched attributes such as threat classifications or customer tiers, reducing noise in expensive tools like Microsoft Sentinel or CrowdStrike.

recent_posts.title: Test network paths with TCP, UDP, and ICMP in Datadog
recent_posts.summary: A guide to choosing between TCP, UDP, and ICMP protocols for network path testing, explaining the trade-offs of each. TCP is suited for reliability-focused apps due to connection state tracking, retransmission, and handshaking, but can introduce HoL blocking and RTO latency. UDP is better for high-speed, real-time traffic like video streaming. ICMP is simpler but more likely to be rate-limited by firewalls. The post also covers SYN vs. SACK strategies for TCP traceroute tests and demonstrates how Datadog Synthetic Monitoring's Network Path tests let you configure and schedule protocol-specific traceroute tests with hop-by-hop visualizations.

recent_posts.title: How to investigate cloud credential compromise with Bits AI Security Analyst
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of how AI-assisted security investigation works in cloud environments, using a real-world scenario of a compromised AWS IAM credential. The post covers four investigation stages: detecting behavioral anomalies (sudden SNS/SES API calls from a user with 60 days of stable history), analyzing API call patterns (single source IP, Boto3 user agent, anonymous proxy flagged by threat intel), mapping attacker goals (enumeration of SNS/SES endpoints suggesting a phishing campaign setup), and generating a final threat classification. Bits AI Security Analyst automates the time-intensive correlation steps—log analysis, threat intel lookups, behavioral baselining—so analysts can focus on containment decisions like revoking access keys and auditing CloudTrail logs.

recent_posts.title: Identify and fix code issues faster with Datadog’s Azure DevOps Source Code integration
recent_posts.summary: Datadog's Azure DevOps Source Code integration connects Azure Repos directly into Datadog, enabling code-aware observability across APM, CI Visibility, Code Security, and Test Optimization. Key capabilities include surfacing vulnerabilities and code quality issues from connected repositories, correlating APM traces and stack traces with source code snippets for faster root cause analysis, posting automated PR comments highlighting new vulnerabilities or flaky tests, and enforcing quality/security standards via PR Gates that block merges until defined criteria are met. The integration reduces tool-switching and shifts issue detection earlier in the SDLC.

recent_posts.title: Centralize observability management with Datadog Governance Console
recent_posts.summary: Datadog Governance Console is a centralized interface for managing observability usage, configuration, and hygiene at scale. It provides a Total Org Usage summary to track active users, dashboards, monitors, and product adoption across teams. Per-product insights (e.g., for Log Management) help identify inefficiencies like unused pipelines or untagged assets. A catalog of automated controls handles detection, notification, and enforcement — for example, revoking dormant API keys — with scoped rollouts to manage risk. The goal is to shift governance from reactive cleanup to proactive standards enforcement.

recent_posts.title: Manage service tracing across hosts with Single Step Instrumentation rules
recent_posts.summary: Datadog's Single Step Instrumentation (SSI) automatically instruments all services on a host, but teams often need finer control over which services generate traces. Instrumentation rules let you define conditions based on process attributes (working directory, executable, runtime language, OS) to either allow or block tracing for specific services. Rules can be deployed centrally via Remote Configuration without SSH access or redeployment, or exported as config files for stricter change-control environments. This allows teams to exclude noisy workloads like batch jobs and cron tasks from tracing, reducing unnecessary trace volume and cost while keeping full instrumentation for critical services.
